queries.name: TwistedVersion
queries.doc:
The Twisted version installed in the environment.

We have different workarounds in place for different versions of Twisted.
queries.query: which installed Twisted release is detected so version-specific workarounds can be chosen

queries.name: TestReport
queries.doc:
Basic test report object (also used for setup and teardown calls if
they fail).

Reports can contain arbitrary extra attributes.
queries.query: result object for a test run phase, including setup and teardown failures, with extra attributes

queries.name: ApproxNumpy
queries.doc: Perform approximate comparisons where the expected value is numpy array.
queries.query: fuzzy equality check when the expected value is an ndarray

queries.name: deduplicate_names
queries.doc: De-duplicate the sequence of names while keeping the original order.
queries.query: remove repeated entries from a list of strings while preserving first-seen order

queries.name: locate_config
queries.doc:
Search in the list of arguments for a valid ini-file for pytest,
and return a tuple of (rootdir, inifile, cfg-dict, ignored-config-files), where
ignored-config-files is a list of config basenames found that contain
pytest configuration but were ignored.
queries.query: find the ini configuration file and root directory from command line arguments, noting skipped config files

queries.name: catching_logs
queries.doc: Context manager that prepares the whole logging machinery properly.
queries.query: context manager that attaches a log handler and sets level during a block

queries.name: safe_exists
queries.doc: Like Path.exists(), but account for input arguments that might be too long (#11394).
queries.query: check whether a path exists without crashing on overly long filenames

queries.name: is_async_function
queries.doc:
Return True if the given function seems to be an async function or
an async generator.
queries.query: detect whether a callable is a coroutine function or async generator

queries.name: copystat
queries.doc:
Copy permission,  last modification time,
last access time, and flags from src to dst.
queries.query: copy file permissions, timestamps and flags from one path to another

queries.name: CollectReport
queries.doc:
Collection report object.

Reports can contain arbitrary extra attributes.
queries.query: result object produced when gathering tests from a file or node, with arbitrary extra attributes

queries.name: Directory
queries.doc:
Base class for collecting files from a directory.

A basic directory collector does the following: goes over the files and
sub-directories in the directory and creates collectors for them by calling
the hooks :hook:`pytest_collect_directory` and :hook:`pytest_collect_file`,
after checking that they are not ignored using
:hook:`pytest_ignore_collect`.

The default directory collectors are :class:`~
queries.query: base collector that walks a folder and creates collectors for its files and subfolders

queries.name: absolutepath
queries.doc:
Convert a path to an absolute path using os.path.abspath.

Prefer this over Path.resolve() (see #6523).
Prefer this over Path.absolute() (not public, doesn't normalize).
queries.query: turn a path into an absolute normalized one without resolving symlinks

queries.name: get_param_argkeys
queries.doc: Return all ParamArgKeys for item matching the specified high scope.
queries.query: list parametrized argument keys for a test item at a given scope

queries.name: format_explanation
queries.doc:
Format an explanation.

Normally all embedded newlines are escaped, however there are
three exceptions: \n{, \n} and \n~.  The first two are intended
cover nested explanations, see function and attribute explanations
for examples (.visit_Call(), visit_Attribute()).  The last one is
for when one explanation needs to span multiple lines, e.g. when
displaying diffs.
queries.query: escape newlines in assertion failure messages while keeping special nested-block markers

queries.name: HelpAction
queries.doc:
An argparse Action that will raise a PrintHelp exception in order to skip
the rest of the argument parsing when --help is passed.

This prevents argparse from raising UsageError when `--help` is used along
with missing required arguments when any are defined, for example by
``pytest_addoption``. This is similar to the way that the builtin argparse
--help option is implemented by raising SystemExit
queries.query: argparse action that aborts parsing early when help flag is given, avoiding missing argument errors

queries.name: doctest_namespace
queries.doc:
Fixture that returns a :py:class:`dict` that will be injected into the
namespace of doctests.

Usually this fixture is used in conjunction with another ``autouse`` fixture:

.. code-block:: python

    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
    def add_np(doctest_namespace):
        doctest_namespace["np"] = numpy

For more details: :ref:`doctest_namespace`.
queries.query: fixture providing a dictionary of names made available inside docstring examples

queries.name: recwarn
queries.doc:
Return a :class:`WarningsRecorder` instance that records all warnings emitted by test functions.

See :ref:`warnings` for information on warning categories.
queries.query: fixture that captures all warnings raised during a test for later inspection

queries.name: fnmatch_ex
queries.doc:
A port of FNMatcher from py.path.common which works with PurePath() instances.

The difference between this algorithm and PurePath.match() is that the
latter matches "**" glob expressions for each part of the path, while
this algorithm uses the whole path instead.

For example:
    "tests/foo/bar/doc/test_foo.py" matches pattern "tests/**/doc/test*.py"
    with this algorithm, but not with PurePat
queries.query: match a filesystem path against a glob pattern using the full path including double-star

queries.name: ExitCode
queries.doc:
Encodes the valid exit codes by pytest.

Currently users and plugins may supply other exit codes as well.

.. versionadded:: 5.0
queries.query: enumeration of the process exit statuses returned by the test runner

queries.name: MoreQuietAction
queries.doc:
A modified copy of the argparse count action which counts down and updates
the legacy quiet attribute at the same time.

Used to unify verbosity handling.
queries.query: argparse action that decrements verbosity when the quiet flag is repeated

queries.name: try_makedirs
queries.doc:
Attempt to create the given directory and sub-directories exist.

Returns True if successful or if it already exists.
queries.query: create a directory tree and report whether it exists afterward without raising

queries.name: ensure_deletable
queries.doc: Check if `path` is deletable based on whether the lock file is expired.
queries.query: decide if a directory can be removed by checking whether its lock file has expired

queries.name: Config_invocation_dir
queries.doc:
The directory from which pytest was invoked.

Prefer to use :attr:`invocation_params.dir <InvocationParams.dir>`,
which is a :class:`pathlib.Path`.

:type: LEGACY_PATH
queries.query: legacy property returning the working directory from which the test tool was launched

queries.name: safe_getattr
queries.doc:
Like getattr but return default upon any Exception or any OutcomeException.

Attribute access can potentially fail for 'evil' Python objects.
See issue #214.
It catches OutcomeException because of #2490 (issue #580), new outcomes
are derived from BaseException instead of Exception (for more details
check #2707).
queries.query: read an attribute returning a default if accessing it raises any error

queries.name: resolve_pkg_root_and_module_name
queries.doc:
Return the path to the directory of the root package that contains the
given Python file, and its module name:

    src/
        app/
            __init__.py
            core/
                __init__.py
                models.py

Passing the full path to `models.py` will yield Path("src") and "app.core.models".

If consider_namespace_packages is True, then we additionally check upwards in the hie
queries.query: find the top-level package directory and dotted module name for a python file

queries.name: ConfigValue
queries.doc:
Represents a configuration value with its origin and parsing mode.

This allows tracking whether a value came from a configuration file
or from a CLI override (--override-ini), which is important for
determining precedence when dealing with ini option aliases.

The mode tracks the parsing mode/data model used for the value:
- "ini": from INI files or [tool.pytest.ini_options], where the only
  sup
queries.query: holds a setting value along with whether it came from file or command line override

queries.name: resolve_fixture_function
queries.doc:
Get the actual callable that can be called to obtain the fixture
value.
queries.query: obtain the actual callable to invoke to produce a fixture's value

queries.name: FunctionDefinition
queries.doc:
This class is a stop gap solution until we evolve to have actual function
definition nodes and manage to get rid of ``metafunc``.
queries.query: temporary placeholder item class standing in for a function node used during parametrization

queries.name: catch_warnings_for_item
queries.doc:
Context manager that catches warnings generated in the contained execution block.

``item`` can be None if we are not in the context of an item execution.

Each warning captured triggers the ``pytest_warning_recorded`` hook.
queries.query: context manager capturing warnings during a test and firing a hook for each one

queries.name: ExceptionInfo
queries.doc: Wraps sys.exc_info() objects and offers help for navigating the traceback.
queries.query: wrapper around caught exception data that helps navigate and format the traceback

queries.name: evaluate_condition
queries.doc:
Evaluate a single skipif/xfail condition.

If an old-style string condition is given, it is eval()'d, otherwise the
condition is bool()'d. If this fails, an appropriately formatted pytest.fail
is raised.

Returns (result, reason). The reason is only relevant if the result is True.
queries.query: evaluate a skip or expected-failure condition, either string expression or boolean, returning result and reason

queries.name: ApproxTimedelta
queries.doc:
Perform approximate comparisons where the expected value is a
datetime or timedelta.

Requires an explicit tolerance as a timedelta for abs, or a float for rel.
Relative tolerance is not supported for datetime comparisons.
queries.query: tolerance-based comparison for dates and time durations requiring explicit absolute or relative tolerance

queries.name: TruncationBudget
queries.doc:
Per-explanation budget for truncating assertion output.

``max_lines`` / ``max_chars`` mirror the ``truncation_limit_lines`` /
``truncation_limit_chars`` ini values: a positive limit bounds that
dimension; ``0`` leaves it unbounded (the limit is disabled).
queries.query: limits on number of lines and characters when shortening assertion failure output

queries.name: PytestDeprecationWarning
queries.doc: Warning class for features that will be removed in a future version.
queries.query: warning category signaling a feature scheduled for removal in a future release

queries.name: record_testsuite_property
queries.doc:
Record a new ``<property>`` tag as child of the root ``<testsuite>``.

This is suitable to writing global information regarding the entire test
suite, and is compatible with ``xunit2`` JUnit family.

This is a ``session``-scoped fixture which is called with ``(name, value)``. Example:

.. code-block:: python

    def test_foo(record_testsuite_property):
        record_testsuite_property("ARCH", "P
queries.query: fixture to add a custom property element to the root of the XML test report

queries.name: get_user
queries.doc:
Return the current user name, or None if getuser() does not work
in the current environment (see #1010).
queries.query: get the login name of the current user, handling environments where lookup fails

queries.name: num_mock_patch_args
queries.doc: Return number of arguments used up by mock arguments (if any).
queries.query: count how many function parameters are consumed by mock patch decorators

queries.name: create_new_paste
queries.doc:
Create a new paste using the bpaste.net service.

:contents: Paste contents string.
:returns: URL to the pasted contents, or an error message.
queries.query: upload text to an online pastebin service and get back its link

queries.name: ensure_extended_length_path
queries.doc:
Get the extended-length version of a path (Windows).

On Windows, by default, the maximum length of a path (MAX_PATH) is 260
characters, and operations on paths longer than that fail. But it is possible
to overcome this by converting the path to "extended-length" form before
performing the operation:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file#maximum-path-length-limitation
queries.query: convert Windows path to long-path prefix form to bypass the 260 character limit

queries.name: pytestconfig
queries.query: fixture giving tests access to the global configuration object for the whole session

queries.name: traverse_fixture_closure
queries.doc:
Statically traverse the fixture dependency closure in DFS order starting
from initialnames, yielding all requested fixture names (argnames).

Each argname is only yielded once.
queries.query: depth-first walk of fixture dependencies yielding each required fixture name once

queries.name: OverrideIniAction
queries.doc:
Custom argparse action that makes a CLI flag equivalent to overriding an
option, in addition to behaving like `store_true`.

This can simplify things since code only needs to inspect the config option
and not consider the CLI flag.
queries.query: argparse flag action that also sets a configuration option, acting like a boolean switch

queries.name: resolve_collection_argument
queries.doc:
Parse path arguments optionally containing selection parts and return (fspath, names).

Command-line arguments can point to files and/or directories, and optionally contain
parts for specific tests selection, for example:

    "pkg/tests/test_foo.py::TestClass::test_foo"

This function ensures the path exists, and returns a resolved `CollectionArgument`:

    CollectionArgument(
        path=Path(
queries.query: parse a command line test path with optional double-colon selectors into file path and names

queries.name: Testdir
queries.doc:
Similar to :class:`Pytester`, but this class works with legacy legacy_path objects instead.

All methods just forward to an internal :class:`Pytester` instance, converting results
to `legacy_path` objects as necessary.
queries.query: legacy-path flavored wrapper around the plugin testing helper for writing and running tests in temp dirs

queries.name: parse_warning_filter
queries.doc:
Parse a warnings filter string.

This is copied from warnings._setoption with the following changes:

* Does not apply the filter.
* Escaping is optional.
* Raises UsageError so we get nice error messages on failure.
queries.query: convert a warning filter string into its components without applying it, raising usage errors on bad input

queries.name: FDCapture
queries.doc:
Capture IO to/from a given OS-level file descriptor.

snap() produces text.
queries.query: redirect and record output of a low-level file descriptor as text

queries.name: CallSpec
queries.doc:
A planned parameterized invocation of a test function.

Calculated during collection for a given test function's Metafunc.
Once collection is over, each callspec is turned into a single Item
and stored in item.callspec.
queries.query: planned parameter set for one generated invocation of a parametrized test

queries.name: TerminalRepr
queries.doc:
Base class for terminal representations -- pieces of data that display
themselves to a terminal.
queries.query: base class for objects that know how to print themselves to the console

queries.name: module_name_from_path
queries.doc:
Return a dotted module name based on the given path, anchored on root.

For example: path="projects/src/tests/test_foo.py" and root="/projects", the
resulting module name will be "src.tests.test_foo".
queries.query: compute dotted import name for a file relative to a root directory

queries.name: traverse_node
queries.doc: Recursively yield node and all its children in depth-first order.
queries.query: depth-first generator walking a tree node and all its descendants
